releases.t: A New Morning, Changing Weather (25th Anniversary Edition)
info: Celebrating the 25th anniversary of A New Morning Changing Weather as an incendiary combination of joyous musical abandon and astute political commentary that is designed to agitate the People AND their booties.

Building upon familiar themes of resistance firmly established on their debut offering, Dennis Lyxzén (former Refused frontman) delivers his scathing brand of political invective with so much musical glee that you might not notice he's trying to foment a revolution! The sound is a fresh and passionate mixture of Soul, Garage, and New Wave, but you can always hear the underpinnings of post-hardcore experimentation bubbling under. ""Up For Sale"" and ""Capitalism Stole My Virginity"" demonstrate that the group have pop sensibilities while ""A Body Treatise"" and ""Born Into A Mess"" expose their darker more intense side. The limited-edition reissue on Yellow & Black split color vinyl also includes a newly created insert including never-before-seen photos and retrospective from the band.

info: Recorded live at New York’s Cellar Cafe on June 14, 1964, Prophecy captures Albert Ayler’s groundbreaking trio with Gary Peacock and Sunny Murray at a pivotal moment in the evolution of free jazz. Ferocious, spiritual, and deeply expressive, the performance introduced compositions like “Ghosts” and “Spirits” in some of their earliest recorded forms, documenting the raw intensity and emotional force that would define Ayler’s legacy. Prophecy Completed expands upon the original album with an additional LP featuring the complete performance for the first time in this format, presenting a fuller picture of this historic session. Newly remastered by Dave Gardner, this deluxe edition continues Org Music’s ongoing archival partnership with the Albert Ayler Estate and restores one of the essential documents of avant-garde jazz history.

releases.t: Blue Moon Over Paris - ORTF Recordings 1963-1968
info: Two never-before-released complete sets by the unforgettable Art Blakey’s Jazz Messengers are presented here. The first, recorded in 1963 at the iconic Olympia Theatre in Paris, features a stellar lineup: Freddie Hubbard on trumpet, Curtis Fuller on trombone, Wayne Shorter on tenor saxophone, Cedar Walton on piano, Reggie Workman on bass, and the leader himself on drums. Highlights include an impressive arrangement of Henry Mancini’s “Moon River” and an extraordinary take on Duke Ellington’s “Caravan.” The second set, taped in 1968 at the equally renowned Salle Pleyel, also in Paris, finds Blakey joined by Bill Hardman on trumpet, Julian Priester on trombone, Billy Harper on tenor saxophone, Ronnie Mathews on piano, and Lawrence Evans on bass. Among the many highlights are an extended performance of the rarely heard “Blues for Eros” and a dazzling version of Bobby Timmons’ “Moanin’.” Transferred from the original tape reels preserved at INA and restored and mastered by Matthew Lutthans at The Mastering Lab, this limited-edition 180-gram 2-LP set includes an extensive insert featuring rare photographs and specially prepared liner notes.

info: This is how good a live album Rock Spectacle is: even though “Brian Wilson” had been released as a studio track back in 1992, it took the rollicking performance on this 1996 release to make the song a hit. But, in retrospect, it’s not that surprising; Barenaked Ladies were and are great on stage (you can hear the connection they have with their audience throughout this recording), so the success of Rock Spectacle totally makes sense. Indeed, this album really represented their breakthrough in the US, and teed up their ascent to superstardom with its Stunt follow-up. For its vinyl debut on its 30th anniversary, we’ve remastered the album for vinyl and pressed 3500 copies on orange vinyl for worldwide distribution, complete with printed inner sleeve. releases.t: Across The Alps - The Lugano & Pescara Concerts
info: This release marks the first appearance of these historic trio performances by Bill Evans, recorded in Lugano, Switzerland, in 1967 and in Pescara, Italy, in 1969. Evans is joined by bassist Eddie Gomez on both recordings, with Arnie Wise and Marty Morell alternating on drums. The Lugano set offers a particularly rare opportunity to hear Wise’s interplay with Evans, as this trio configuration was seldom recorded. Transferred from the original tape reels and restored and mastered by Matthew Lutthans at The Mastering Lab, this limited-edition 180-gram 2-LP set includes an extensive insert featuring rare photographs and liner notes by acclaimed jazz critic and author Marc Myers, along with statements by Marty Morell, Sylvie Courvoisier, and others.

info: Twenty years after its original release, Passover has been re-recorded and reimagined through the lens of two decades of growth - as a band, as musicians, and as people. These songs have lived many lives since 2006. Shaped across thousands of performances around the world, each track has evolved into a living, breathing organism - changing subtly night after night, year after year. These new recordings document that evolution. Working alongside producer Dave Sardy (Oasis, LCD Soundsystem, Modest Mouse), The Black Angels returned to Passover not to recreate it, but to fully realize what the songs have become twenty years later. The result is a heavier, deeper, and more expansive recording: bigger riffs, richer textures, deeper low end, and a renewed sense of atmosphere and intensity that reflects the band as they exist today - while preserving every ounce of the raw power and spirit that defined the original album. Originally written and recorded during the Iraq War, the themes and message behind Passover feel more urgent and relevant now than ever before. Two decades later, these songs still speak to cycles of violence, disillusionment, resistance, and humanity’s ongoing struggle against oppression - a reminder that history continues to repeat itself. This is not a nostalgia piece. It’s Passover transformed by twenty years of experience, perspective, and sound.

releases.t: The Preacher In Paris - Live at The Elysee Montmartre
info: Bobby Womack was one of the most distinctive voices in soul music—singer, songwriter, and guitarist whose work bridged gospel, R&B, and funk. From his early days with The Valentinos to his classic solo recordings for United Artists Records, Womack shaped the sound of modern soul with raw emotion and fearless creativity. His songs have influenced generations of artists across soul, rock, and hip-hop. Recorded in Paris on March 15, 1976, Live at the Élysée Montmartre captures Womack at the height of his powers, delivering the intensity and charisma that made him a legendary stage performer. A powerful, previously unheard document of one of soul music’s most enduring and influential artists.
Transferred from the original tape reels preserved at INA, this limited-edition 180-g 2-LP set includes an extensive insert featuring rare photographs and specially prepared liner notes.

info: 2001’s self-titled David Axelrod was originally issued on Mo’Wax and is long out of print on vinyl. The genesis of the full length is a “lost” album recorded in the late ‘60s, in the same period as his landmark release, Songs of Experience. It was meant to be an Electric Prunes album, the third of a trilogy for Reprise, based around the legend of Faust. He took his stalwart crew of LA session musicians, including drummer Earl Palmer, bassist Carol Kaye and guitarists Howard Roberts and Pete Wyant, and recorded rhythm tracks. He cut them to an acetate for review. The project was shelved, but he kept that acetate. In the late 90s, after meeting Mo’Wax boss James Lavelle through his work with DJ Shadow, Axelrod agreed to write, arrange and record what would have been the completed orchestra and horn tracks at the same Capitol Studios he had recorded at in the 1960s. He augmented the album with two tracks written specifically for the release, no longer about a cursed bargain, but as a reflection of a life in music, and a life, few knew then, full of triumph and tragedy. Now-Again’s Egon sat in on those Capitol sessions and, 26 years after their recording, has partnered with the Axelrod Estate to present this music anew.

Beyond the acclaimed recordings he has made as a solo artist and with his influential bands—The Three O’Clock, Jellyfish, The Grays, and TV Eyes—Falkner’s extraordinary talents have been sought out by an impressive roster of artists including Beck, Paul McCartney, Aimee Mann, St. Vincent, Noel Gallagher, Brendan Benson, and Air. Born in San Francisco and raised in Southern California, Falkner was a classically trained piano prodigy whose musical gifts emerged at an early age. He first gained widespread recognition as a member of the pioneering Paisley Underground band The Three O’Clock, whose final album, Vermillion, was released on Prince’s Paisley Park Records. Soon afterward, he joined the legendary power-pop outfit Jellyfish before forming the highly influential pop-rock group The Grays alongside Jon Brion. Yet Falkner’s true artistic destiny lay in his solo work. In 1996, he signed with Elektra Records and released two critically celebrated albums: Presents Author Unknown and Can You Still Feel? Written, produced, and performed by Falkner himself, both records showcased his remarkable ability to blend sophisticated songwriting, inventive arrangements, and flawless musicianship. Decades later, they remain touchstones for fans and fellow musicians alike. Omnivore Recordings is proud to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Falkner’s landmark debut, Presents Author Unknown. For this special edition, Falkner returned to the original multitrack tapes to create an all-new remix, revealing greater depth, punch, and sonic detail while remaining faithful to the spirit of the original release. Side 4 of this double album contain the outtake “My Home Is Not A House” and three 4-track demos of songs from the album. Pressed on opaque red and green vinyl, this deluxe anniversary edition also features extensive new liner notes from Falkner, reflecting on the album’s enduring significance and the creative motivations behind revisiting and remixing the record three decades later. Thirty years after its original release, Presents Author Unknown remains a shining example of timeless songwriting and fearless musical craftsmanship. This new remix not only reaffirms the album’s lasting brilliance—it reminds us why Jason Falkner continues to be regarded as a musician’s musician, an artist whose creativity, vision, and passion remain as vital as ever.

Known for having been the inspiration for The Replacements’ iconic song “Left of the Dial" and for her work with Tres Chicas, the Salt Collective, Let’s Active and alongside artists including Alejandro Escovedo, Jeffrey Dean Foster, and Velvet Crush, Blakey also was a remarkable and passionate songwriter herself. But this has been, until now, somewhat “hidden in plain sight.” This collection, curated by Chris Stamey and carefully remastered for this release, will change that. Evocative rockers such as “Rest” and “The Beauty of 23” from Glory Fountain, her 1990s collaboration with guitarist John Chumbris, sit beside Americana tracks like “Sweetwater” (with Tres Chicas) and “Immigrant Heart”, and dream-rock such as “In the Shadow of the Moon” with R.E.M’s Mike Mills and “Love Finds (Allumente)” with her husband, violinist Ecki Heins, the “Stolen German”. info: Released in time to mark what would have been Marianne Faithfull’s 80th birthday on December 29th 2026, this exceptionally rare live recording from her 1983 tour of Canada and America captures a powerful performance from Marianne at the height of her early ’80s resurgence following the release of her acclaimed multi-platinum, Grammy-nominated album Broken English. Recorded at the Wax Museum in Washington D.C. on October 2, 1983, Marianne and her band perform a diverse setlist drawn from her 1979 comeback Broken English, 1981 follow-up LP Dangerous Acquaintances and the then-recently released A Child’s Adventure. The concert also features the previously unreleased track “Rising”. Transferred from the original analogue tapes and restored and mastered by Andrew Batt, the recording delivers exceptional clarity while preserving the raw intensity of the original performance. Released with the support of the Marianne Faithfull estate, the limited-edition 180g 2LP set features music across three sides and on side D an etching in Marianne’s handwriting of an excerpt from William Blake’s poem ‘The Tyger’, which she recites in “Eye Communication”. Originally released on March 1, 1980, Masayoshi Takanaka's first live album, SUPER TAKANAKA LIVE!, returns for RSD Black Friday 2026 Recorded during his nationwide tour in December 1979, the album captures the excitement and electrifying energy of Takanaka's live performances just a few years after his solo debut. Featuring many of his signature compositions, the performances deliver an intensity and spontaneity that take the original studio recordings to new heights. A defining feature of the album is its dynamic live arrangements and the exceptional musicianship of Takanaka and his band. Classics including "Blue Lagoon,” “Explosion,” “Ready To Fly” and “Kurofune (Black Ship)” are brought to life through thrilling improvisation, powerful ensemble playing, and an unmistakable concert atmosphere that showcases Takanaka's extraordinary talent as a guitarist. Among the album's highlights, the live version of "READY TO FLY" stands as one of the most celebrated performances of Takanaka's career. Its soaring guitar solos, infectious energy, and remarkable band interplay have made it a fan favorite and one of the defining live recordings in Japanese jazz fusion. Serving as the foundation for later acclaimed live releases such as OCEAN BREEZE and THE RAINBOW GOBLINS STORY LIVE AT BUDOKAN, SUPER TAKANAKA LIVE! remains an essential live album that perfectly captures the excitement, virtuosity, and joyful spirit of Masayoshi Takanaka's performances. This special RSD Black Friday 2026 edition, pressed on translucent vinyl, offers both longtime fans and new listeners the opportunity to experience one of the greatest live albums in the history of Japanese jazz fusion. The debut of the most talked about jazz pianist to come out of New Orleans.

Oscar Rossignoli, with origins in Honduras, has resided in New Orleans for over a decade and has released two unaccompanied solo piano recordings (Inertia and Levitations), three recordings with the trio Extended, and has lent his unmistakable touch to the efforts of a vast array of New Orleans artists. His recent trio recording, Mar Adentro, is a major step in Rossignoli’s evolution.

The trio album, which features bassist Lex Warshawsky and drummer Peter Varnado, opens in stunning fashion with some rapid virtuosic piano playing on Cuban composer Ernesto Lecuona’s “Gitanerías,” a classical piece that Rossignoli proceeds to mold into modern jazz. The title cut “Mar Adentro” (literally, “the sea inside”) paints a cinematic picture, starting with an evocation of ocean waves before unfolding into a deeply, introspective performance.

Stop Pretending captures The Pandoras at their fiercest—fusing snarling punk energy with retro girl-group swagger—and this expanded edition finally gives fans the full picture. Notably, The Pandoras lineup featured future The Muffs members Kim Shattuck and Melanie Vammen, whose songwriting chemistry and unmistakable edge would later help define an entirely new era of alternative rock. Pressed across two LPs, the collection features the original album newly remastered by original producer Bill Inglot, sourced from the best available recordings to deliver sharper punch and deeper grit than ever before. But the real treasure lies in the vault: a handpicked selection of previously unreleased bonus tracks, rare B-sides, and long-lost recordings—carefully curated from the archives by the band’s remaining members—showcasing their evolution and unfiltered studio energy. Housed in a beautifully designed gatefold sleeve, this anniversary edition includes rare archival photos, liner notes detailing the band’s legacy, and insights into the making of the record during a pivotal moment in underground rock history.

Before Ruben Blades became one of the most influential voices in Latin music, he was shaping his artistic identity in Panama through a series of rare and largely unknown recordings that remained hidden from most fans, collectors, and even longtime followers for decades. El Inicio brings together, for the first time ever, ten early recordings from the late 1960s featuring Ruben as vocalist with Los Salvajes del Ritmo, Nacho Molino y su Conjunto, and Orquesta Dimeños — years before New York, Fania, and the global recognition that would change salsa forever.

These recordings capture the foundation of the storytelling, urban narrative, genre fusion, and social perspective that would later redefine Latin music through his groundbreaking work with Fania and Seis del Solar. Moving between boleros, guarachas, and guaguancos, the collection also reveals a little-known side of Ruben Blades as a powerful sonero and romantic vocalist, offering collectors and fans an unprecedented look into the formative years of a musical visionary.

Pressed on 160g colored vinyl, El Inicio features fully restored and remastered audio by Frank Merritt at London’s legendary The Carvery Studio, alongside brand-new artwork built around a never-before-used archival photograph of Ruben Blades. More than a compilation, this is a historic archival release — the missing first chapter in the story of one of salsa’s greatest innovators.

Studio One DJ’s 2 is the classic Studio One collection from Soul Jazz Records. Described as ‘The University of Reggae’ by Chris Blackwell, Studio One and founder Clement ‘Sir Coxsone’ Dodd are by far the most-important names in the history of reggae music. Originally released in 2006 and out of print for more than 15 years, this is the first ever color vinyl edition of this classic album. This album is newly fully remastered for vinyl by Jason Goz at Transition and pressed at Optimal in Germany. The album features classic and rare cuts from some of the finest toasters ever to come out of Jamaica – tracks by DJ greats Dennis Alcapone, Lone Ranger, Prince Jazzbo, King Stitt, alongside super-rare tracks from artists such as Bobby Jackie, Jah Jesco and Little Joe, all recorded under Clement ‘Sir Coxsone’ Dodd’s supervision at the legendary Jamaican record company. Musical backing comes from the legendary in-house bands – The Skatalites, The Sound Dimension, Soul Vendors and Soul Defenders – who provide the classic Studio One rhythms so influential in the history of Reggae. As well as eighteen killer tracks compiled by Mark Ainley (Honest Jons), the album comes with sleevenotes by Steve Barrow (Blood and Fire/Rough Guide to Reggae) and photography by Dennis Morris, making this another essential Studio One Reggae release for connoisseurs of Reggae and newcomers alike. The collection is lauded for its quality and is often considered one of the best releases from Soul Jazz's Studio One series. Exclusive one-off pressing on heavyweight double transparent blue vinyl with download code. Exact reproduction of the original artwork.

info: Studio One Dub 2 brings together some of the finest dubs from the legendary Studio One Records, Kingston, Jamaica. Dub music was the creation of a generation of brilliant recording studio engineers in Jamaica. Most of the original Studio One dub albums released during the 1970s were mixed by Coxsone Dodd himself, using the moniker "Dub Specialist", although many talented engineers worked the board at the Brentford Road studio over the years (including Sylvan Morris, Syd Bucknor, and Overton "Scientist" Brown). Throughout the 1970s, these mixes became more sophisticated and atmospheric. The cuts here demonstrate that Studio One's contribution to the innovative musical form of dub was substantial and go straight to the head of listeners who feel that the only centers for dub were studios such as King Tubby's, Lee Perry's Black Ark, Channel One, or Joe Gibbs’. The tracks on this compilation are taken from this period in the 1970s when dub was the cutting-edge of Jamaican music studio production. Most of them are the dub-version flip-sides of rare Jamaican 45s. Sleevenotes are by Michael E. Veal, celebrated author of Dub: Soundscapes and Shattered Songs in Jamaican Reggae. New one-off pressing sky-blue double vinyl limited-edition for RSD Black Friday. Out of print for over 10 years. First ever color vinyl edition. "Dub is the music of the studio engineers and the sound-system rulers. Studio One Dub cannot help but to serve as loving tribute to this giant of a man who not only defined popular music for the isle of Jamaica, but for the world over, his innovations laying the foundations for hip-hop, dance and post-rock."-- Pitchfork "Soul Jazz unearths a new bag of lost, rare, and essential dub gems from Jamaican cornerstone label Studio One. A fresh taste of timeless music.” --XLR8R

This is the first time the music of the quartet with Gilberto is available on vinyl.

info: On Audiotree From Nothing, Thrice strip the gloss from key tracks off their 2025 album Horizons/West for a 4-song EP recorded Jan 2026 at Chicago’s Audiotree studios. Reworking four standout cuts, the band double down on the grit and immediacy that’s defined their 2025 tour run. Tracks like “Vesper Light” showcase Dustin Kensrue’s elastic vocals, moving from Thom Yorke-like hush to scorched-earth grit—a reminder that Thrice still thrive in the raw. The band will be on tour all year including playing large cap rooms opening for Jimmy Eat World in June/July and My Chemical Romance at the Hollywood Bowl on Halloween. No guitarist sounds like the late, great Tom Verlaine. His career-long pursuit of the perfect, effect-free guitar tone set him apart from his peers right off the bat; combine that with his vaunted vibrato technique, self-taught, free jazz-influenced sensibility, and the slow burn and build architecture of his solos, and there really is no mistaking his fretwork for anybody else’s. Verlaine’s singular instrumental and songwriting prowess certainly came through on his studio recordings, both with Television and solo. But it was in live settings that his improvisational genius really shined. Fortunately for us, it turns out, as one might expect from an artist whose interests ranged widely from literature and modern art to music, that Tom was something of a collector. Therefore, we at Real Gone Music are truly thrilled to present the first of what we hope will be a series of release from his extensive archives: a double-LP collection of COMPLETELY UNRELEASED live performances drawn from four different New York shows spanning the years of 1996 to 2006. Along the way you’ll hear songs taken from his solo albums ranging from his first self-titled release to The Wonder, Flash Light, Words from the Front, Around, and Songs and Other Things, plus three songs new to his discography. Compiled and mastered by Verlaine’s long-time engineer and band-mate Patrick Derivaz, with artwork contributions by his partner, the artist Jutta Koether, and liner notes by Derivaz, Koether, David Fricke, Jimmy Rip, Alan Licht, and Tony Shanahan, Live NYC 96-06 is a key contribution to the Tom Verlaine catalog and an absolute must for his fans and guitar heads alike.
Limited to 3000 copies worldwide on sea blue vinyl!

info: To commemorate forty years since its original release, USA for Africa presents a special 7” vinyl release of the newly digitally remastered “We Are the World” specifically for RSD Black Friday, with proceeds continuing to support the organization’s ongoing humanitarian mission. Beyond the cultural significance of the song itself, the charitable nature of the project provides a strong foundation for the release. The combination of the milestone anniversary and the fact that this would mark the first reissue since the original 1985 release makes it a highly collectible and meaningful offering for both longtime fans and new audiences. “We Are the World” remains one of the most recognizable and culturally impactful songs ever released, featuring iconic artists including Michael Jackson, Lionel Richie, Stevie Wonder, Bruce Springsteen, Diana Ross, Cyndi Lauper, and many more.

info: Before dominating the Grammys and defining the sound of modern R&B, Victoria Monét delivered two of her most intimate, foundational projects: Life After Love, Pt. 1 and Life After Love, Pt. 2. Released individually in 2018, these twin EPs capture a pivotal chapter in Monét’s evolution as a solo artist, establishing the lush vocal arrangements, cinematic production, and razor-sharp songwriting that would later captivate the world. Now, for the first time ever, both transformative projects are combined into a single physical release, debuting exclusively on vinyl for RSD Black Friday 2026.

The dual project charts a complete emotional arc, chronicling the delicate journey from heartbreak to self-actualization. Part 1 delves into the raw vulnerability and quiet introspection of a breakup’s immediate fallout, anchored by sultry, unfiltered anthems like "Freak." Part 2 turns the page toward rediscovery, blooming into an exploration of newfound confidence and sensuality through standout cuts like "New Love" and the shimmering, bass-heavy fan favorite "Ass Like That." Seamlessly bridging pain and empowerment across its tracklist, the combined collection showcases Monét's innate ability to translate personal grief into universal, groove-heavy solace.

By pressing these two landmark EPs together on wax, this release offers long-time fans and vinyl collectors the ultimate way to experience Monét's early masterwork as a unified narrative. It stands as a long-overdue physical grail, celebrating the resilient spirit of an artist taking back her narrative—and serving as a reminder that the best music often blooms from the ashes of heartache.
